scraped.scraped_description: Planning services designed by councils for councils.

name: Open Digital Planning
tagline: Planning services designed by councils for councils — a community of Local Planning Authorities transforming England's digital planning system
project_type: Government digital services platform / civic infrastructure
org_type: Government-backed community programme (MHCLG); transitioning to independent nonprofit
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 — Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
political_units: local government (Local Planning Authorities in England)
funding_model: Digital Planning Improvement Fund (£50,000 grants per LPA)
known_funders: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG)
last_funding_event: 2025 — 49 additional Local Planning Authorities joined via Digital Planning Improvement Fund; 171 total LPAs now supported
dependency_risks: sustained government funding for MHCLG Digital Planning Programme
legislation needed to mandate data standardisation

news_articles.headline: Open Digital Planning: a cross-sector partnership to transform local planning services

academic_citations.title: The Digital Twin: Realizing the Cyber-Physical Production System for Industry 4.0
A digital twin smart city for citizen feedback

policy_outcomes.description: PlanX and BOPS deployed by 100+ Local Planning Authorities across England, cutting planning application processing times by approximately 30% per application
171 Local Planning Authorities now publishing planning data on the Planning Data Platform via the Digital Planning Improvement Fund

outcome_methodology: self-reported processing time reductions from participating councils
published_performance_metrics: 30% reduction in processing time per application (self-reported)
documented_limitations: England-specific legislation and planning system; limited international transferability
requires council political will and digital capability
failure_modes: low council adoption outside early cohorts
inability to achieve legislative mandate for data standards
governance_model: Community of Local Planning Authorities co-owned by members; MHCLG provides delivery guidance; transitioning to independent not-for-profit entity jointly owned by councils
curation_criteria: Open contribution model for councils; product decisions made collaboratively by participating Local Planning Authorities; technical contributions governed via GitHub contribution guidelines
contributor_governance: Councils co-own services and contribute to product direction; product decisions made collaboratively by participating LPAs
disparity_tracking: Equity considerations embedded in council co-design process; focus on ensuring digital access across diverse council sizes and digital maturity levels; monitoring adoption across urban and rural authorities
community_ownership: Moving toward council-owned not-for-profit; councils currently co-direct product strategy

government_partnerships.partner: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG)
government_partnerships.description: Primary funder and coordination partner for the Digital Planning Programme
Co-host of Local Government Innovation Hackathon

ai_involvement: Partnered with i.AI (UK Government Incubator for Artificial Intelligence) for hackathon; AI use in planning data processing under exploration
